moved: The 1st: the forward tees 9-12 m off the line (pads on the line hid the landing area from the Summit tee) and the fairway starting 16 m past the Terrace tee; the fall along the shelf evened out (it was all in the last 100 m, so a crest hid the fan); the fan widest at the approach (alike.mjs read it as a spindle); a fourth bunker, right of the green; the green's spine moved off the pin (7.5% at the cup).
The 2nd and 4th: no kerb across a par 3's carry or in front of any green (the 1.6 m lip hid the flag from the tee on the 2nd, and on the 5th it stood across the approach).

The 3rd: a half-pipe where the drives land (banks rising from the line), the valley floor level 22 m either side by the stream (the lay-up targets sat on 20% banks, now 19 m and 16 m off the line); wider, the widest fairway of the nine (mean 63 m); five bunkers, two of them across the second-shot ground.
The 4th: the ground falls 9 m from the tee to the valley's lip (it rose 5.6 m and hid the Needle from every tee); the forward tees 12-13 m off the line.

The 5th: where the ridge meets the eastern cliff's foot the ground is no higher than the green (it stood 3 m above the approach); the tips 20 m behind the tee (at 30 m it was on the Needle's rim); a second greenside bunker.

The 6th: the face 16 m further on, 262-278 m out (287-304 yd), so a 150 mph drive stops 9 yd short of its foot; a grass ramp up it beside the pilgrim stair, 18 m wide, 248-300 m, 28% at its steepest: the hourglass's neck (without it the fairway was two pieces, a second broken form next to the 5th, which alike.mjs refuses).
The 7th: the green's spine moved off the pin (4% at the cup); a second bunker, long left.
The 8th: the tips beside the tee, 34 m back and 22 m left (behind the tee stands the alcove's corner); the forward tees off the line; a second greenside bunker.

The 9th: the first bank moved up to the Summit tee's lip (from 80 m back on a level tier nothing below the bank was in view). It crosses the line 7 m in front of the tee, runs down the line's left side between the 9th and the 8th green, then east below that green. The Terrace tee 38 m right of the line (the old spot, 40 m left, was nearer the green than its card said); the second tier's fairway wider; no sand (the courtyard's paving and walls).

Everywhere: tee pads 0.25 m proud (they were 0.4) and never built out over a drop; the alcove's back and end walls are fins of rock 26-30 m thick (their tops ran on 260 m as a plateau 92 m up, over the 9th green); the cairn beside the 8th green (it stood on the 9th's Ledge tee); more greens with two bunkers or none (two-thirds had exactly one; spread.mjs asks five at most).
open: The 9th's views. From the Summit tee the first tier is in sight, but not the green, and not the golden roof: the 8th green's bluff stands in that line. From the tiers the green is out of sight (a green just below a 15 m bank shows only from the bank's lip). Keep it so (the bold drive blind at a marker, the one blind tee shot of the nine; from the first tier a blind wedge at the golden roof)? Or a true switchback: each tier runs down a ramp at its turn to the next, so the safe route always sees the next tier? Or lower the 8th green 4 m so the golden roof shows from the 9th tee?

The 9th's bold drive: of twelve 150 mph drives at the golden roof, 7 finish in the courtyard on paving, 3 in scrub, 2 in rough, none on the green. The green takes a pitch, not a running drive. Is that the risk you want on the drivable par 4?

The 5th's numbers. Short of the notch (249 yd) leaves 260 yd; over it (a 290 yd carry, about 265 at sea level) leaves 198 yd, not the wedge the layout doc expected. The bold line gains 62 yd. Keep, or move the notch 40 m nearer the green so the carry leaves a short iron?

The 6th's face: nobody in the gate flies it. A tour drive carries 290 yd to the face's foot (287) and stops in the rough on it. Move the face 10 m nearer so a tour drive flies it (a 150 mph drive would then run to its foot), or keep it as a wall for the second shot, the ramp the way up?

Where the tools read a form differently from the card: the 3rd reads a spindle (the form sheet's bowl is nearly as wide as long; the 3rd's is 435 m by 114); the 5th reads a table top (the notch's far side), so the bold height forms count four (5, 6, 8, 9; two or three wanted); the 8th reads a hillside bench (the terrace wall crosses its landing area); the 9th reads broken (its third tier's fairway joins the green). Keep the cards' names, or reshape so the tools agree?
